HISTORY AND PHYSICAL (H&P) NOTE

Patient: Sandra Bullock  DOB 20 Feb 1958  Encounter: Remote video with Dr Smith  
Date: [date of consultation not provided]

History:
• Presenting complaint: 5-day history of troublesome dry cough and continuously streaming nose.  
• Onset/Duration: Began ~5 days ago; symptoms persist.  
• Character & Progression:  
  – Cough: Dry, occurs every 20–30 min, no sputum, no haemoptysis, no chest pain, no dyspnoea or pleuritic pain.  
  – Nasal discharge: Constant, green-tinged. No epistaxis.  
• Associated symptoms: Subjective fever with alternating chills; has not measured temperature. Generalised myalgias. One brief episode of diarrhoea at onset (resolved). No sore throat, ear pain, headache, visual changes, rash, vomiting, or current diarrhoea.  
• Triggers/Relievers: Lemsip (paracetamol-containing) 2–3 sachets/day provides temporary throat relief.  
• Previous episodes: None stated.

Past Medical History:
• Type 2 diabetes mellitus.  
• Hypertension.  
• No chronic lung disease reported.  
Allergies:
• No known drug allergies.  
• Occasional mild hay-fever.
Medications:
• Metformin – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Lisinopril – patient believes “200” (likely 20 mg); route/frequency not documented.  
• Lemsip cold remedy (contains paracetamol) 2–3 sachets daily as needed.  
Social / Family:
• Lives with partner and dog; works as an office manager.  
• Denies smoking; drinks “the odd sherry.”  
• No travel or occupational exposures mentioned.

Physical Examination:
(Remote consultation – no direct exam)  
• General: Appears well on video, conversant.  
• Respiratory: Patient denies dyspnoea, wheeze, or chest pain.  
• HEENT: Reports green nasal discharge; no facial pain; denies sore throat or ear pain.  
• Skin: No rashes.  
• Neurological: No headaches or visual changes.  
• Vital signs: Not recorded.

Impression:
Acute viral upper respiratory tract infection / viral bronchitis most likely.  
DDx (consistent with transcript):  
1. Acute viral URI (common cold/influenza-like illness) – typical constellation of cough, rhinorrhoea, myalgias, subjective fever.  
2. Post-viral or early bacterial sinusitis – suggested by green discharge; monitor for progression.

Management Plan:
• Symptomatic care: Continue Lemsip but avoid any additional paracetamol-containing products. Maintain hydration and rest.  
• Monitoring: Purchase a thermometer; check temperature regularly.  
• Red-flag advice: Re-consult or seek urgent care if any of the following occur: temperature ≥ 37.5-38 °C persisting or spiking, worsening cough, development of purulent sputum, haemoptysis, new chest pain, shortness of breath, or persistent green/bloody nasal discharge.  
• Diabetes/HTN care: Ensure routine diabetes and blood-pressure reviews with GP; no current glucose‐monitoring equipment at home.  
• Medications: Daytime cough syrups not recommended; may use small amount at night if cough prevents sleep.  
• Follow-up: Contact physician if no improvement in 7–10 days or sooner if red-flag symptoms appear; antibiotics may be considered if bacterial infection suspected.

Patient Summary:
66-year-old woman with diabetes and hypertension presents with 5-day dry cough and green rhinorrhoea, mild systemic symptoms, and no respiratory compromise. Clinical picture suggests viral URI; provided symptomatic advice and safety-net instructions.

Key Takeaways:
1. Buy a thermometer today and monitor temperature twice daily.  
2. Continue current Lemsip only; avoid other paracetamol products.  
3. Seek medical review if fever persists, cough worsens, sputum/blood appears, or breathing becomes difficult.

Next Steps:
• Obtain thermometer and begin temperature log.  
• Self-monitor symptoms for the next week; re-consult if worsening or no improvement.  
• Arrange routine diabetes and blood-pressure check-ups with GP.
